ops.title: Session guard owner lifts run on grants (PR #278): accepted finder risks
ops.body: PR #278 (feat/sessions-grants, stacked on #277) moves the session guard's owner lifts onto grants: sessions.close {terminal}, sessions.launchctl {service}, sessions.task-stop {task}. Each is judge-less, evidence is Rulings (a cc-notes answer naming the value as a whole name, updated_at before the acting session), one use per ruling+scope across all trees, replay window 2 min. sessions.close also takes CreatedHere: this session's transcript shows a lone bare orca terminal create --json naming the handle, or an orca-launch.sh call that printed terminal=<handle> while ~/.claude/scratch/orca-launch/*/<lane>.terminal.json was written. It also needs no dispatch in worker-list across all Runs (ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE dropped) and a tui-idle wait plus an idle prompt on screen. A lift requires the call to run once: first command, top level, only pipe successors. Accepted finder risks: (1) owner ruling and self-created idle are separate lifts, not cumulative, by the owner's ruling; (2) a deliberately forged and backdated launch receipt is out of scope, since the guard targets agent mistakes; (3) launchctl remove is liftable like bootout. Test hazard found: tests/test_pack_sessions.py overrides() passed env={} so the request lost CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR, and grant writes went to the real ~/.claude/state/hooks/grants.db. Fixed by carrying the state dir; the one leaked row (tree s1) was deleted.
